- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent auction supply; dampen forecast by 1–3% per event beyond 10.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility clustering — use rolling 7-day volatility as adjustment multiplier.
